summary: How ExxonMobil, Shell, Chevron and the American Petroleum Institute were warned from 1959 on, and told by their own scientists by the 1980s, that fossil fuels drive climate change, then spent decades funding denial and lobbying against regulation.

evidence.note: story begins with Teller's 1959 warning to the oil industry
1968 Stanford report commissioned by the API warns of warming
Exxon senior scientist warns executives in 1977 and 1978
Global Climate Coalition propaganda campaign against Kyoto
long segment on CEO Lee Raymond and the Do No Harm ads
Exxon funding of denier think tanks and black ops budget
Tillerson, New York shareholder case and the alias email account
Tillerson's February 2020 Houston speech closes the timeline
2018 spending against state ballot initiatives and for candidates
Shell internal report released by a Dutch news outlet

notes: Chevron is named in the title but gets only a short late segment, so it is secondary; ExxonMobil carries the story. Shell is the main co-subject (Anglo-Dutch, HQ in NL at the time), hence NL in setting; harm is global. API and Global Climate Coalition appear as keywords given the 5-subject cap.
